questions.question: What output format should you download from Meshy.ai for use in a Three.js project?
options: FBX with separate texture files
OBJ with MTL material file
GLB (binary GLTF with embedded textures)
STL (stereolithography mesh)
questions.explanation: GLB is the best choice for web projects — it bundles the mesh and all PBR textures into a single binary file that Three.js's GLTFLoader handles natively.

questions.question: What is 'retopology' in the context of AI-generated 3D models?
options: Applying a new texture to a model
Rewriting the mesh with cleaner, more optimized geometry and polygon flow
Scaling the model to a different size
Converting a GLB file to OBJ format
questions.explanation: AI-generated meshes often have messy, irregular triangle distributions. Retopology is the process of rebuilding the surface with cleaner geometry — important for rigging, animation, and performance.

questions.question: Which part of a Meshy.ai text prompt most improves output quality?
options: Using all lowercase text
Specifying a short, vague description like 'a sword'
Describing shape, material, style, and use case in detail
Adding the word 'photorealistic' at the end
questions.explanation: The more specific your prompt (shape, material, style, scale, purpose), the better the AI can match your intent. Compare 'a sword' vs 'a weathered iron longsword with a golden crossguard, low-poly game-ready style'.

questions.question: What is a negative prompt in AI 3D generation?
options: A prompt that reduces the quality on purpose
A list of things to include in the model
A description of features to AVOID in the output
The prompt used to delete a generated model
questions.explanation: A negative prompt tells the AI what NOT to generate — e.g., 'blurry, low quality, deformed, watermark'. It helps steer the model away from common failure modes.

questions.question: After loading a GLB from Meshy in Three.js, the model appears off-center. What's the fix?
options: Delete the model and regenerate it
Change the camera position to match the model's offset
Compute the model's bounding box, find its center, then subtract that from the model's position
Scale the model by 0.01 to normalize coordinates
questions.explanation: AI-generated models often have their origin at a corner or bottom of the mesh, not the center. Use new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(model) to compute the bounding box, then model.position.sub(center) to reposition it.
